concepts.def: If P up and TR up, demand is inelastic.
PED = infinity, any rise drops Q to zero.

walkthroughs.body_html: 1) Calculate % change in Q. 2) Calculate % change in P. 3) Divide Q% by P%. Example: Price £10 → £12 (+20%). Quantity 100 → 80 (−20%). PED = 20/20 = 1.0 — unit elastic.

If demand is inelastic (PED < 1), raising price raises total revenue (price up more than quantity falls). If elastic (PED > 1), raising price LOWERS revenue. So firms with inelastic goods (utilities) push prices up; luxury sellers compete on price.
Bus fare £2, daily riders 1,000 → TR = £2,000. Fare rises to £2.20 (+10%), riders fall to 950 (−5%). PED = 5/10 = 0.5 inelastic. New TR = £2.20 × 950 = £2,090. Revenue UP £90. Smart move.
